title: Functional Food Potential of Magnolia liliiflora Leaves: Chemical Profiling of Bioactive Lignans and Their Anti-Inflammatory Effects in LPS-Activated Microglia.
authors: Ponce-Zea, Jorge-Eduardo; Che, Yun-Hui; Jung, Gwan-Young; Mai, Van-Hieu; Le, Minh-Thi-Tuyet; An, Jin-Pyo; Oh, Won-Keun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究木兰叶木脂素的抗炎作用，仅用分子对接预测与NF-κB靶点结合，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Background/Objectives: Neuroinflammation is a key contributor to neurodegenerative diseases. Magnolia liliiflora Desr. is a traditional medicinal plant with therapeutic potential; however, its bioactive constituents and mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify active compounds from M. liliiflora leaves that inhibit inflammatory responses in microglial BV-2 cells. Methods: Anti-inflammatory activity was assessed by measuring nitric oxide (NO) production in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated BV2 microglial cells. UPLC-qTOF MS/MS-based metabolite profiling combined with bioactivity-guided analysis was used to identify candidate biomarkers, which were subsequently isolated and structurally characterized. Network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were performed to predict potential molecular targets and mechanisms of action. The effects on NF-kappaB signaling and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression were further validated by Western blot analysis. Results: Two previously undescribed lignans (1 and 2) and five known lignan derivatives (3-7) were isolated from the leaves of M. liliiflora. At 20 microM, compounds 1, 3-5, and 7 exhibited moderate inhibitory effects on nitric oxide (NO) production in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated BV2 microglial cells, with 23%, 33%, 69%, 56% and 49% inhibition, respectively, and no detectable cytotoxicity. Notably, an ethyl acetate-derived enriched subfraction showed 97% inhibition of NO production at 10 microg/mL, suggesting potential synergistic activity of M. liliiflora lignans. Network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses predicted interactions between the isolated lignans and NF-kappaB pathway-related targets, thereby guiding subsequent experimental validation. Both compounds significantly reduced the expression of iNOS and COX-2 and suppressed LPS-induced activation of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway in a concentration-dependent manner, as confirmed by Western blot analysis. Overall, the results demonstrate that M. liliiflora leaves are a source of bioactive lignans that attenuate microglial activation by inhibiting NO production and key inflammatory mediators, effects that are associated with the suppression of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. Conclusions: This study identified bioactive lignans from M. liliiflora leaves and demonstrated their anti-inflammatory activity in microglial cells. The findings establish the structural identities of the active compounds and confirm that M. liliiflora leaves are a valuable source of lignans with therapeutic potential for neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative disorders.
abstract_zh: 背景/目标：神经炎症是神经退行性疾病的关键诱因。紫玉兰（Magnolia liliiflora Desr.）是一种具有治疗潜力的传统药用植物；然而，其生物活性成分和作用机制尚不清楚。本研究旨在从紫玉兰叶片中鉴定抑制小胶质细胞BV-2炎症反应的活性化合物。方法：通过测量脂多糖（LPS）刺激的BV2小胶质细胞中一氧化氮（NO）的产生来评估抗炎活性。采用UPLC-qTOF MS/MS代谢物谱分析结合生物活性导向分析来鉴定候选生物标志物，随后对其进行分离和结构表征。通过网络药理学和分子对接分析预测潜在的分子靶点和作用机制。通过Western blot分析进一步验证对NF-kappaB信号通路以及诱导型一氧化氮合酶（iNOS）和环氧合酶-2（COX-2）表达的影响。结果：从紫玉兰叶片中分离出两种此前未描述的木脂素（1和2）和五种已知的木脂素衍生物（3-7）。在20微摩尔浓度下，化合物1、3-5和7对脂多糖（LPS）刺激的BV2小胶质细胞中一氧化氮（NO）产生表现出中等抑制效果，抑制率分别为23%、33%、69%、56%和49%，且未检测到细胞毒性。值得注意的是，一种乙酸乙酯衍生的富集亚组分在10微克/毫升浓度下对NO产生表现出97%的抑制率，提示紫玉兰木脂素可能具有协同活性。网络药理学和分子对接分析预测了分离的木脂素与NF-kappaB通路相关靶点之间的相互作用，从而指导了后续的实验验证。Western blot分析证实，两种化合物均显著降低iNOS和COX-2的表达，并以浓度依赖性方式抑制LPS诱导的NF-kappaB信号通路激活。总体而言，结果表明紫玉兰叶片是生物活性木脂素的来源，这些木脂素通过抑制NO产生和关键炎症介质来减弱小胶质细胞活化，其效应与NF-kappaB信号通路的抑制相关。结论：本研究从紫玉兰叶片中鉴定了生物活性木脂素，并证明了它们在小胶质细胞中的抗炎活性。研究结果确定了活性化合物的结构特征，并证实紫玉兰叶片是木脂素的宝贵来源，对神经炎症和神经退行性疾病具有治疗潜力。
